01 — The Standard

Made in
Madeira.
Forged
for history.

He arrived as a wiry teenager with a step-over and a promise, and left as the most decorated scorer the sport has produced — the first man to score at six World Cups, the first to 200 international caps, the only man past 900 goals still chasing more.

985 official senior goals. 1,343 appearances. Five Ballon d'Or. The numbers are not the story. The story is that every single one of them had to be taken — by repetition, by obsession, by refusing to be finished.

05 — The Farewell Lisbon · 5 November 2026
“The day has come for me to hand back the number 7 shirt of our national team. I never felt it belonged to me alone — but for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it, and carrying it into stadiums all around the world. Today the time has come to pass it on to the future.”
Cristiano Ronaldo — farewell letter to Portugal

He left the national team as its most-capped player and record scorer: 234 appearances, 146 goals, 45 assists and three major trophies — the first of them in 2016, when Portugal won a major tournament for the first time in its history. He will continue at club level with Al-Nassr.

06 — The last number

The only record left

0 of 1,000

Fifteen goals separate Cristiano Ronaldo from a thousand for club and country — a line no man in the history of the sport has crossed. He is still playing.

07 — End of the archive

The number
stays on.

Nine hundred and eighty-five goals. Three trophies with Portugal. A record 234 caps and 146 goals that may stand for a generation. The shirt has been handed back — but No.7 never really leaves.
